question.text: When a hydrogen atom going from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> emits a photon, its recoil speed is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></math>_______. (Use: mass of hydrogen atom <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>27</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>, charge of electron <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>)</mo></math>

solution.text:
According to the above diagram, the difference in energy between the two states is given by

ΔE=-3.4 eV--13.6 eV=10.2 eV

The formula to calculate the recoil speed is given by

v=∆Emc   ...1

From equation (1), it follows that

v=10.2 eV×1.6×10-19 J1 eV1.6×10-27 kg×3×108 m s-1=3.4 m s-1=175 m s-1

Therefore, x=17.
